text: In machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE), the Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) acquisition function proposes the next variant to test by...
choices: Always proposing the variant with the single highest model-predicted fitness, ignoring uncertainty
Combining the predicted mean fitness with a weighted measure of prediction uncertainty (mean + k times uncertainty) to balance exploration and exploitation
Randomly sampling variants uniformly across all of sequence space
Selecting only variants identical to the current best-characterized variant
explanation: UCB explicitly combines the surrogate model's predicted mean fitness with a scaled uncertainty term (mean + k times uncertainty), and the tunable parameter k controls the balance between exploring uncertain regions and exploiting known-good ones. Always choosing the highest predicted fitness with no uncertainty term describes the 'greedy' strategy rather than UCB; uniform random sampling ignores the surrogate model entirely; and restricting proposals to variants identical to the current best would not explore any new sequence space at all.
